answers.answer: Office attrition is resolved simultaneously: roll one die per held office card and add one for each fatigue on that card; the Chairman also adds one. Modified 1–2 does nothing, 3–4 adds fatigue, and 5+ retires. On retirement, move the member to Pensioners, flip the card into Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to supply.
answers.evidence: London Season — “Simultaneously roll one die for each held office card. Add one per fatigue on that card; Chairman also adds one. Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire. Move retiree to Pensioners, flip card into Vacant Offices, return its fatigue to supply.”

answers.answer: Only players who retired at least one pensioner may take or discard one display card. They act in descending actual total retirement spending; ties go to most total windows, including new prizes, then clockwise from the PM. The acting player may peek at display blackmails. No chosen or discarded card is replaced during selection; if the display empties, skip all remaining eligible players immediately. Then discard all remaining display cards and refill exactly three, with prestige faceup and blackmail facedown, even if nobody took a card. Return all unused Pensioners to their supplies.
answers.evidence: London Season — “Players who retired at least one pensioner must each take or discard one display card, in descending actual total retirement spending. Ties: most total windows, including new prizes, then clockwise from PM.” “Do not replace a chosen/discarded card during selection. If the display becomes empty, immediately skip every remaining eligible player.” “discarding all remaining cards and refilling exactly three: prestige faceup, blackmail facedown, even if nobody took a card.” “Return all remaining Pensioners to their supplies.”

answers.answer: At the start of the Family phase, check where the opportunity marker was. Choose a main family action once, or take it twice if the marker already matched it; then move the marker to the chosen main action. Only the latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action after the main action; the extra action is not doubled and does not move the marker. With four vacant offices, Enlist Writer gains one additional writer once this turn, so a doubled Writer action can place three writers total.
answers.evidence: Family — “Check where your opportunity marker was at phase start.” “Choose a main family action: take it once, or may take it twice if the marker already matched it.” “Place/move the opportunity marker onto your chosen main action.” “After the main action, only the latest passed extra-action law may grant its extra action. This extra action is never doubled by the marker and never moves the marker.” Enlist Writer row: “With at least four vacant offices, place one additional writer once this turn, so a doubled Writer action can place three total.”

answers.answer: After all family actions, while both Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one, repeating while both remain. Pieces in Court are Company shares. If there is no Debt, slide the remaining applicants as far right as possible while preserving their order. Seeking a share pays the bank; it never pays family cash into Company treasuries.
answers.evidence: Family — “After all family actions, if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one. Repeat while both remain. Pieces in Court are Company shares. With no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible, preserving order. Seeking a share never pays family cash into Company treasuries.”

answers.answer: Fill vacant offices in ascending number on their card backs. The designated hirer chooses a candidate and moves that member into the office; the member’s owner gets the card. When promoting an officeholder, transfer its fatigue to the new card and insert its old card, vacant, into ascending hiring order. For an ordinary own-family hire, every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool must give verbal consent. If no candidate exists or the hirer is vacant, skip the office; it stays vacant and takes no actions, including hiring. Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt from Nepotism consent.
answers.evidence: Hiring — “Fill vacant offices in ascending number on their card backs.” “When promoting an officeholder, transfer its fatigue to the new card and insert its old card, vacant, into ascending hiring order.” “Own-family hiring needs verbal consent from every other player in that office’s candidate pool, EXCEPT that a Chairman election never requires Nepotism consent. Commander appointments are also exempt.” “If no candidate exists, or the hirer is vacant, skip the office; it stays vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.”

answers.answer: The former Chairman first announces the number of shares needed for a pure majority, meaning more than half of current shares. Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one of the winner’s Company shares into the Chairman slot and give them the title marker. That piece still counts as a share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in firms. If nobody gets support, the former Chairman picks any shareholder, including themself, without Nepotism consent. If Court is empty, the former Chairman automatically returns; if needed, place a member from supply or, if necessary and possible, from a prize (losing its VP). If that is impossible, there is no Chairman.
answers.evidence: Chairman election — “Former Chairman first announces the number of shares needed for a pure majority (more than half of current shares). Any shareholder may campaign; first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins.” “It still counts as a share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in firms.” “If no candidate gets support, former Chairman picks any shareholder including self; no Nepotism consent.” Empty Court fallback sentence.

answers.answer: For a Company-office check, first commit resources and cash: all cash comes from the acting office’s treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, then roll and use the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and may be retried if resources and office-specific limits allow; 5–6 is catastrophic, ends that office’s actions, returns the officeholder to supply, discards fatigue and flips the card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander and firm procedures modify this. Do not take a dead action with no effect or chance of success, such as trade with no ship or deploying without dice just to trigger officer losses.
answers.evidence: Success checks — “First commit resources/cash: all cash for a Company-office check comes from that acting office’s treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, then roll. Use lowest die: 1–2 success; 3–4 failure, retry if resources and office-specific limits allow; 5–6 catastrophic failure, no more office actions, return officeholder to supply, discard fatigue and flip card into Vacant Offices.” “You cannot take a dead action with no effect or chance of success...”

answers.answer: The Chairman may add up to three Debt freely, each adding £5 to Balance. Each additional advance requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares, counting the Chairman, and Debt may never pass the track end. Then allocate all Balance to other offices’ treasuries, reducing Balance by each transfer. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved while respecting the total borrowing rules; cash already in offices stays there for their use.
answers.evidence: Chairman — “May add up to three Debt freely, each +£5 Balance. Each additional advance requires consent of players controlling majority Company shares (Chairman counts); never pass Debt track end. Then allocate all Balance to other offices’ treasuries, lowering Balance by each transfer. May interleave borrowing and allocation while respecting total borrowing rules. Cash already in offices remains there for their use.”

answers.answer: The Manager of Shipping must spend treasury money until £2 or less remains. Leasing an extra ship costs £2; fitting a ship from a shipyard costs £3 and needs no owner consent; buying a Company ship costs £5 and is allowed only if no ships remain on shipyards. Place each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China once that office exists. Extra ships serve only until Refresh.
answers.evidence: Manager of Shipping — “Must spend treasury until £2 or less remains. Lease extra ship £2; fit ship from shipyard £3 without owner consent; buy Company ship £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Place each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China once office exists. Extra ships serve only until Refresh.”

answers.answer: For Trade, declare the home region and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 from the President’s treasury buys one die, and each declared nonhome region subtracts one die. A failed attempt may be retried during operations if affordable; catastrophe removes the President; a President can succeed at most once per turn, and failed attempts and retries stay within that President’s uninterrupted opportunity. Successful capacity is one order per ship in that Presidency’s sea zone, and Trade does not exhaust ships. Fill as many orders as possible within declared regions: the first writer goes to the home port; each later order must extend this Trade’s connected route. Writers from another Presidency cannot extend it. Writers do not cap capacity: after using all available writers, continue with filled-order tokens, which extend the same route. No President may fill another President’s home region, even if that office is vacant. Add each order’s printed value to Balance, or half rounded down if a firm already filled it this turn; the President gets £1 from the bank per order and writer owners get £1 per placed writer.
answers.evidence: Presidency operations and Trade — complete declaration, dice, retry/success limit, capacity, route, writer/token, home-region and payment sentences quoted/paraphrased above.

answers.answer: A Commander may target their own Presidency’s home, any associated region, or a region bordering an associated region. They cannot target another home region or another Presidency’s Company-controlled region. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order for Deploy to have an effect. Exhaust each selected officer or regiment for one die and each local alliance for its printed dice; subtract the combined strength of the target and all other regions in its empire, counting the target only once. After each attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments never cause officer-loss rolls.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy — numbered steps 1–3, including valid targets, die resources, empire penalty and after-each-attempt officer losses.

answers.answer: On success, take loot from the bank equal to £4 per target tower plus any faceup loot modifier, with a minimum of the surviving officers used in this attempt plus £1 for the Commander. Distribute repeatedly in cycles: first £1 for the Commander and £1 per used surviving Commander-family officer; then £1 per used surviving officer of each other family clockwise; then £1 per used regiment and per used local-alliance piece to the bank, regardless of alliance strength. The Commander gets one trophy per target tower. After loot and trophies, remove the target tower and dome (and, if it was a capital, every matching empire flag in India); open all target orders and remove all target unrest; on a new conquest put the loot/control token symbol-side up above the associated President’s box, put the Governor overlay in the conquered region, and put only the Governor card in Vacant Offices. If the Elephant faced outward from the conquered region, move it fully inside. If the target was already Company-controlled, there is no new Governorship. On catastrophe, the Commander returns half their family’s trophies rounded up and returns to supply; exhausted officers still check losses, and the Commander has no office card to vacate.
answers.evidence: Deploy success payout-cycle and control tables; catastrophe sentence; Commander member has no office card.

answers.answer: A Governor takes the printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty and then reduces the pool by one regardless of result. On success, take £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, and choose exactly one benefit: build one ship stage, commission one regiment, or tax £2 to Company Balance or the associated President’s treasury. Each successful Build places a partial ship in the Governor’s region if none is there; a later successful Build completes it into the sea zone associated with that President. A commissioned regiment goes to that President’s Army. Each Tax after the first this turn adds unrest in the region. Every unsuccessful roll adds one regional unrest, and catastrophe also removes the officeholder under the normal rule. Repeat using the shrinking pool until the Governor stops, has no dice, or suffers catastrophe.
answers.evidence: Governors: Administer — printed-pool paragraph, result table, options table, repeat sentence.

answers.answer: Company expenses reduce Balance by £1 per existing Debt, each officer or regiment in an Army, and each ship in sea zones, including China; exclude Commanders. If Balance is insufficient, take £5 emergency loans. Each loan advances Debt one only while a track space remains; at maximum Debt, continue taking loans without advancing Debt. Newly added emergency Debt has no extra expense this turn. After the loans, set Balance to zero; one or two loans lower Standing one, and three or more lower it two. Compare remaining Balance with expectations under current Standing and lower Standing one if Balance is below them. Then the Chairman may pay any affordable number of dividends: each dividend costs one cash per Company share and pays each owner £1 per share, including the Chairman. If total dividend cash is strictly greater than expectations, advance Standing one.
answers.evidence: Revenue — Expenses, Expectations and Dividends numbered procedure.

answers.answer: For an attack on a Company region, resolve the primary Crisis first, then secondary Rebellions in Bombay, Madras, Bengal Army order; within each Presidency its Commander chooses the order of associated regions. A primary normal Crisis uses normal Invasion/Rebellion strength plus unrest in its target. A primary Foreign Invasion uses only the ordinary attack die, without unrest. Each secondary Rebellion uses only the number of unrest cubes there, with no event modifier or empire strength. If the associated Commander is occupied, that Commander chooses and exhausts pieces and normal trophy gains/losses apply; if vacant, Military Affairs acts in the Commander’s stead with no trophies; if both are vacant, the Chairman chooses with no trophies. Exhaust active Army pieces equal to Crisis strength, or as many as possible; local alliances provide printed strength once and cannot be split among purposes. If newly exhausted strength equals Crisis strength, the attack fails and defense succeeds: remove all unrest in the region; the actual Commander gains one trophy, while substitute Military Affairs/Chairman gains or loses no trophies. If this defeats a normal primary Invasion, also remove one attacker tower if possible. If the strengths do not equal, the attack succeeds and defense fails, causing Region Loss; a successful primary Invasion also applies empire creation/growth. The summary leaves unresolved how excess indivisible alliance strength is counted in the strength-2-alliance versus strength-1-attack case.
answers.evidence: Attacks on Company, Mounting defense actor/table, printed strength comparison table, unresolved counting boundary.

answers.answer: A vote with support of −1 or less fails: discard the law, resolve a dilemma’s “If Failed” text, and have the Opposition Leader return the token and take the PM dial. The new PM moves the proposed policy one space either direction and resolves that adjacent policy. Zero or higher passes: place the law with passed laws, the PM takes a passed-law token, then resolve the selected policy and immediate law effects. Finally restore all cards used for voting to their regular orientation after either outcome. If the law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring.
answers.evidence: Parliament — Resolution paragraph.

answers.answer: In 1758 and Long 1710, at turn start before London Season, the PM may call the special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. Use ordinary voting procedure and support threshold. The vote has no policy, and the PM may vote against it. On a pass, lower Debt one for every two current Debt, set Standing to S, give the PM a passed-law token, and activate firms. On a failure, increase Company-share scoring value by the Court VP token, up to a maximum of ±3 VP per share; the PM stays in power and the Deregulation law is not discarded. 1813 begins deregulated.
answers.evidence: Setup Standing/Deregulation spaces and Deregulation section result table.

answers.answer: Only a player who manages no firm may form one: return one eligible Company share to supply or flip a workshop to its invested side, flip the family board to its firm-charter side, place a family member as the first firm share, set the Value cube at the leftmost space, and take £5 from the bank into London. To invest in a firm, with manager consent, contribute a Company share or workshop in the same way; the bank pays £5 into London. A firm may have up to ten shares; further investments still add £5 but create no shares. The Chairman share cannot be used, and no Company shares may be used when Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space. Shares created this turn cannot be used even if traded away. Invested workshops never revert, do not give the bonus or Company-failure VP, and remain invested if the firm fails.
answers.evidence: Firms phase investments — form and invest bullet points.

answers.answer: Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt per turn, and only a firm with at least one ship may select a trade strategy; it may select a closed home port. Managers choose secretly; for a trade-zone/home-port strategy they commit a secret bid from London, while Hobnob has no bid, trade or dividends. Reveal bids together, but keep strategies facedown until the associated Presidency begins. Before that Presidency’s actions, matching firms reveal and roll one die per £1 bid, paying the bid to the bank; at least one 1 or 2 allows trade. Firm initiative is ship count minus successful dice, and a successful President’s Trade sets initiative the same way using Presidency ships. After a successful Company Trade, fill by lowest initiative; the President orders ties, so the Company is not automatically first. If the President is vacant or never successfully Trades, firms fill after Commander/Governor opportunities, with Chairman breaking ties. Fill open orders only, up to ships plus one, starting at the strategy home port and tracing that firm’s own filled route; the firm cannot refill its own prior order this turn, but may refill an order filled by a different firm or Company, and Company may refill a firm’s. A previously filled order pays half its listed revenue rounded down. Advance firm Value one space per full £6 added to India treasury this turn.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies and competing trade — strategy table and trade-order/initiative/filling paragraphs.

answers.answer: At Revenue, before Company expenses, each firm pays £1 per charter ship plus the greater of its share count or Value, using either or both firm treasuries. If it cannot pay, it dissolves unless rescued: shares go to Debtor’s Prison for −1 VP each, ships return to their shipyards, its charter flips to the family side, and workshops remain invested. After expenses, the manager may pay dividends from the India treasury only; each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to the manager. A shareholder may waive payment for any number of shares only with both that shareholder’s choice and the manager’s consent. Record total actual cash paid out on the dividend marker. An active non-Hobnob firm paying none records zero; Hobnob keeps its prior marker. Sweep remaining India money into London.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends — expense, dissolution, and dividend paragraphs.

answers.answer: Components are limited, and when a supply runs out, complete as much as possible. Cash, trophy and passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies. Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks are unlimited. All information, including discards and family cash, is public except facedown blackmail and firm strategies/bids while they are temporarily concealed during selection.
answers.evidence: Components — Limits paragraph.

answers.answer: Players may trade enterprises, facedown blackmail, family treasury cash, Company or firm shares, and promise cards. They may not trade officeholders, writers, officers, prizes, spouses, trophies, passed laws, played blackmail, the PM dial or Chairman piece. To transfer a share, return the old owner’s family member and replace it at the share’s location with a member from the receiving family. Played faceup blackmail cannot be traded; blackmail must stay facedown when traded.
answers.evidence: Negotiation table and “To transfer a share” paragraph.

answers.answer: An immediate transfer is binding. A promise of future behavior is nonbinding, except a printed promise card’s guaranteed effect can be called if possible. Promise-card calls follow their printed timing and limits, and no promise calls are allowed during Final Scoring. If simultaneous calls cannot all be fulfilled, the guarantor chooses which to fulfill. A promise card may be traded to a third party or back to its guarantor. Transferred resources cannot activate twice; for example, a workshop that paid during Bonuses does not pay again after being sold during that same phase.
answers.evidence: Negotiation agreement/promise table.

answers.answer: Use the chosen scenario’s player setup cards, adding three extra cards for five players or six for six players, then shuffle and deal evenly. Place every listed holding: take cash and enterprise cards into the player’s area; put each family member in its listed office and give that owner the matching office card; put Company-share members in Court of Directors; put writers, officers and trainees in their indicated Presidency, Army or Training boxes; put Commanders in their Army Commander slots without office cards; and take each shipyard and put its matching ship in the listed sea zone or on its shipyard if unfitted. Each starting luxury gives 2 VP. Shuffle prestige and blackmail together into one deck and deal three cards for the London Season display, prestige faceup and blackmail facedown.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–4.

answers.answer: The game ends after the scenario’s final turn or when Standing reaches failure. Failure is normally immediate; if it occurs during Events in India, finish that phase, and if legislation causes failure, finish the vote before scoring. Once the game is over, stop negotiations, promise calls and playing blackmail unless a card explicitly permits final-scoring use. During all Final Scoring, no negotiations or promise calls are allowed.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions — game end and negotiation restrictions.

answers.answer: For Power, count enterprises and Company shares at their current Power-track rates (the bottom two positions are zero), plus one per passed-law token and trophy, two for the PM, and printed card power from blackmail faceup or facedown and applicable spouses. The highest and second-highest awards are 3/1 VP on final turns 1–3, 5/2 on turns 4–6, and 8/4 on turns 7–8. A tied-first group receives only the lower award each, with no other award; tied second receive none. Highest final VP wins; ties go to most windows, then clockwise from the PM.
answers.evidence: Power award paragraph; Highest final VP wins paragraph.

answers.answer: If the Company survived, add the Court’s current VP value for each Company share; if it failed, subtract that value per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop. Scores can be negative. In the final outcome step, a surviving Company rolls office attrition and retires Pensioners, with no prestige/display cards. If it failed, draw one random Company failure card and resolve its printed consequence. Firm special retirement occurs before ordinary final scoring in either outcome and is not replaced by the failure card.
answers.evidence: Court/workshops; Final retirements/failure card table; Final Scoring order.

answers.answer: Spouses usually add VP, impose permanent restrictions and cannot be transferred. Required enterprise or share trades happen immediately when taking the spouse. Retirement discounts can stack and are personal; each discount is usable once per London Season and once during Final Scoring. Discounts reduce actual spending and therefore prestige display priority. The summary does not enumerate individual spouse restrictions or point effects; those are card-specific.
answers.evidence: London Season — Spouses paragraph; Source boundary.

answers.answer: If a shipyard is returned because of Violet Effingham or an unpaid tax, its fitted ship stays in play. The shipyard cannot be purchased while its matching ship remains in play; it can be purchased after that ship returns.
answers.evidence: London Season — Returned shipyard rule.

answers.answer: Enlist Writer places a family member in any Presidency’s Writers box; with at least four vacant offices, place one extra writer once this turn, allowing three total on a doubled Writer action. Enlist Officer places a member in Officers-in-Training. Purchase Luxury costs £4 to the bank and grants a luxury worth 2 VP while owned, its window icon and social-enterprise status. Purchase Shipyard costs £2 to the bank and places the matching ship unfitted on that shipyard; it is a Shipping enterprise with one vote and a £1 bonus while fitted. Purchase Workshop costs £5 to the bank; it is a manufacturing enterprise with two votes and a £1 bonus, and is worth 1 VP if the Company fails unless invested. Seek Share places a member on an empty Stock Exchange space and pays the bank the queue price (£2, £3, £3, £4 or £5); it is an applicant, not yet a share.
answers.evidence: Family action effects table.

answers.answer: If a family member must be placed and none is in supply, take one from any of that player’s prizes and lose that prize’s printed VP; this also applies to firm-share creation. If no family action is possible, take none and return the opportunity marker to supply.
answers.evidence: Family — forced prize-piece reuse and no-action rule.

answers.answer: If Court is empty, the former Chairman automatically returns. Place a member from supply, or if necessary and possible take one from a prize and lose that prize’s VP. If it is impossible to place the member, there is no Chairman.
answers.evidence: Chairman election — empty Court fallback.

answers.answer: The Chairman chooses the Director of Trade from current officeholders other than the Chairman or a Governor; if all offices are vacant, choose any writer. The Chairman chooses any writer for Manager of Shipping. For Military Affairs, the Chairman chooses a Presidential Commander; if none, any officer; if none, any Officer-in-Training. The Director of Trade chooses a President who is a writer of that Presidency or a Governor associated with it. The associated President chooses a Governor who is a writer or officer in the region; a Commander is not an officer and is ineligible. The Chairman chooses any writer for China Superintendent, immediately when China is created. The Governor General replaces the Director and is hired the same way. Ordinary own-family hiring requires verbal consent from every other player represented in the candidate pool; Commander appointments are exempt.
answers.evidence: Hiring office/candidate table and Nepotism exceptions.

answers.answer: The Director may make repeated Special Envoy checks, paying £1 from the Director’s treasury per die, with no penalty. Each success either opens one closed order in a non-Company region or opens China by placing the Superintendent overlay/card, after which the Chairman immediately hires a writer. After all envoys, the Director may make up to two transfers, each moving one writer or ship between any Presidencies or sea zones (including China if created). The Director cannot transfer while still taking envoys.
answers.evidence: Director of Trade procedure.

answers.answer: Military Affairs may make up to two transfers, each moving one officer or regiment from one Army to another while it remains in the top half. Then assign every Officer-in-Training to the top half of any Army. Finally appoint Commanders: if an Army has a vacancy or a family has more total pieces there than the current Commander’s family, choose among families with the most pieces; move the chosen officer to the Commander slot and return the previous Commander to the top as an officer. A tie with the current Commander’s family does not replace them, and Nepotism does not apply.
answers.evidence: Military Affairs procedure.

answers.answer: Each President chooses the order of that Presidency’s Commander, Governors and Trade, and must allow each position an opportunity, though Commanders and Governors may decline. Each position finishes all its actions before the next begins; Trade may occur before or after another position but cannot interrupt it. If the President is vacant, the Chairman sets the order only and cannot Trade or approve local alliance purchases.
answers.evidence: Presidency operations and Trade — ordering paragraph.

answers.answer: Trade itself never exhausts ships. During Refresh, writers on orders return to their associated Presidency’s Writers box, using dividers to preserve affiliation; filled tokens and Presidency dividers return to supply.
answers.evidence: Presidency Trade sentence; Upkeep and Refresh table.

answers.answer: At the start of Commander operations, before Deploy attempts, request the President’s treasury funds for any printed-price local alliances in the Army; the President must approve. Move purchased alliances to the top/active half. When used for Deploy or defense, exhaust the whole alliance to the bottom half; its strength is usable once that turn and cannot be split among purposes. Refresh exhausts any unused active alliances and does not reactivate them as it does officers and regiments.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy — local alliance paragraph.

answers.answer: To Deploy in an already Company-controlled region to reopen orders or clear unrest, Company defense penalty is zero. No tower remains, so the Commander gains zero tower trophies. With no tower or faceup loot modifier, the minimum loot is surviving participating officers plus £1 for the Commander, distributed normally.
answers.evidence: Deploying in an already Company-controlled region paragraph.

answers.answer: Each successful Build performs one stage. If there is no partial ship in the Governor’s region, that one success places the partial ship there; if a partial ship is already there, that one success completes it into the sea zone associated with the Governor’s President. The two stages therefore require two successes total. A successful Commission regiment places it in the Army associated with the Governor’s President; it has officer-like strength, its loot is paid to the bank, and it does not cause officer-loss rolls.
answers.evidence: Governors: Administer — Build Company ship and Commission regiment table rows.

answers.answer: China is created by a successful Special Envoy or the Envoy to China law; in either case, the Chairman immediately hires any writer. Its treasury holds ships, not cash. Shipping and the Director of Trade may send ships there like any sea zone. Those ships count as Eastern for expenses, events, storms and laws. China acts after Bengal.
answers.evidence: China Superintendent procedure.

answers.answer: The Superintendent may attempt China Trade only once, including a failed attempt, so there is no retry. Roll one die per ship. If Company-controlled regions have no export icon, do not attempt China Trade. On success, count export icons in all Company-controlled regions only: Company Balance receives £4 multiplied by that number, and the Superintendent’s family receives £1 per icon from the bank. Non-Company export icons do not count; the Company payment is not a flat £4.
answers.evidence: China Superintendent — trade eligibility, dice and recipient table.

answers.answer: When the Governor General law creates the office, immediately make all Governors pensioners, remove their overlays and partially built Company ships, and return Governor and Director cards to the box. Replace the Director of Trade with the Governor General, preserving the holder and fatigue, and place its ribbon overlay. No further Governors or overlays are created on conquest; printed Company symbols indicate controlled regions. On region loss, skip Governor Elimination.
answers.evidence: Governor General setup and loss rules.

answers.answer: First add £3 to Balance per Company region. Then the Governor General may attempt Govern repeatedly, paying £1 from the treasury per die with no penalty. Every 6 rolled adds one unrest to each Company region, even on success; failure adds another unrest to every Company region. On success, the Governor General’s family takes £1 from the bank per Company region, then must choose one benefit per region: complete a Company ship into any sea zone, including China; put a regiment into any Army; or put £2 into Balance or any office treasury except the Governor General’s own, adding unrest to a Company region. Multiple Tax choices this turn must place unrest in different regions. At most one successful Govern is allowed per turn.
answers.evidence: Governor General Govern procedure.

answers.answer: Company ships and extra ships are exempt from storm checks. Check player-owned ships in Company fleets in the affected zone; ships assigned to China count as Eastern. Firm ships count in the sea zone on their firm strategy, even though they are on a charter; Hobnob firm ships are exempt. Roll once per eligible ship: 1–2 does nothing; 3–4 adds fatigue or sinks a ship already fatigued; 5–6 sinks it. Return a sunk ship to its shipyard unfatigued.
answers.evidence: Events — Storms eligibility table and roll procedure.

answers.answer: When an order newly closes, return any writer on it to its owner’s supply; flip a filled token to closed. If instructed to close an order in a region where all orders are already closed, Cascade by closing all open orders directly connected to that region’s orders. If a connected order is already closed, close that region’s northernmost open order instead. If none are open, it also Cascades. A region can initiate a Cascade only once per event tile, but can receive multiple Cascades’ effects. At Refresh, writers on orders return to their associated Presidency’s Writers box, while filled tokens and Presidency dividers return to supply.
answers.evidence: Events — Closing orders and Cascades; Upkeep and Refresh table.

answers.answer: Turmoil closes the northernmost open order in the top-stack region, or Cascades if all its orders are closed. Windfall gives owners £1 per writer on orders in the top-stack region and every bordering region. Shuffle makes the Elephant March, then shuffles that tile into the remaining draw stack; separately shuffle the discards and put them on top. If the draw stack is empty, March last instead.
answers.evidence: Events table rows for Turmoil, Windfall and Shuffle.

answers.answer: Leader gives one tower to a sovereign top-stack region. If the top-stack region is dominated, it instead rebels using the printed explosion modifier. March the Elephant only if it was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.
answers.evidence: Events table — Leader row.

answers.answer: If the Elephant is on a border, Peace opens orders connected across its border and adds one tower to each touched non-Company region. If the Elephant is wholly inside a region, instead open all its orders and remove its unrest. Then March the Elephant.
answers.evidence: Events table — Peace row.

answers.answer: In an ordinary Invasion, the sovereign attacker’s whole empire strength plus the event modifier must be greater than the defender’s whole empire strength; equality does not win. On success, replace the defender’s flag with the attacker’s dominated flag, and taking a capital shatters its entire empire. If the attacker had no empire, use a free capital/star flag and matching small flag; if none are available, no new empire or flags form. On failure, the attacker loses one tower.
answers.evidence: Invasion Crisis paragraph.

answers.answer: For a non-Company Rebellion Crisis, compare only the rebelling region’s strength plus the event modifier against its sovereign capital’s strength; other regions of the empire do not count. The rebel must be strictly greater, so a tie does not succeed. On success the actor becomes sovereign, its flag is removed, and all its orders close (Cascade if already closed). On failure, remove one tower from the capital.
answers.evidence: Rebellion Crisis paragraph.

answers.answer: On Region Loss, the Commander returns half their family’s trophies rounded up, then the Commander member returns to supply. Roll once per officer in the associated Army; each 6 removes that officer. Eliminate the Governor by returning its office card to the unused stack, fatigue and member to supplies; remove the Governor overlay, partial Company ship and unrest. Restore the dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion’s specified strength) and the appropriate invasion flag. Return the control token to its region with its £ loot side down and region-symbol side up; future conquest gets no loot modifier and the region loses its Presidency association. An Invasion Crisis closes all its orders (or Cascades if already closed); Rebellion and Foreign Invasion already close them. Standing loss escalates by the number of regions lost so far this turn: first −1, second an additional −2, and so on. If this causes failure, finish Events in India before Final Scoring. One region’s loss does not automatically remove another Company region; resolve each attack and defense separately.
answers.evidence: Region Loss paragraph.

answers.answer: After a successful Invasion Crisis, move the Elephant to the successful capital (Imperial Ambitions); after other Marches, move it to the top-stack region. In a Company region, place it fully inside. In a dominated region, point it toward its sovereign. In a sovereign region, point it across the shape-marked border on that tile. If that neighbor is already dominated by the acting region, choose the first clockwise neighbor that is not; if all neighbors are dominated, use the redirect-arrow shape’s border, pointing toward the empire capital.
answers.evidence: Elephant’s March paragraph.

answers.answer: Roll the storm die to select Foreign Invasion target regions: West targets Bombay, South Madras, East Bengal; all storms means each, and no storms means the top-stack region. For each target, roll an ordinary die for attack strength and resolve Invasion/Company attack. The designer ruling says unrest does not add to the primary Foreign Invasion attack or determine the resulting tower levels; use the ordinary attack die for both attack strength and halving to create towers. On success, close all target orders (Cascade if already all closed), remove the target’s flag and all matching flags if it is a capital, restore the dome if Company-controlled, and set tower strength to half the attack roll rounded down. March with the circle shape only if the Elephant was fully inside a Company region that was invaded.
answers.evidence: Foreign Invasion event row; FAQ Foreign Invasion and unrest ruling.

answers.answer: The PM must draw at least one law, revealing cards one at a time. After one or two ordinary non-dilemma draws, the PM may stop or continue up to three total; choose one revealed law and discard the others. Drawing a dilemma forces its selection and ends drawing immediately. Before voting, move the dial arm clockwise or counterclockwise, stopping at the first policy space matching the chosen law’s bottom icon; that space sets the target and consequence.
answers.evidence: Parliament — law draw and policy selection paragraph.

answers.answer: Under Tax, each family pays £1 to the bank per target it owns; each unpaid target returns to supply, including the Chairman if taxed. Window tax additionally charges each window on enterprises and each family member’s prize, returning the enterprise or prize member if unpaid. Under Bonus, the bank pays each family £1 per target it owns. Under Power, swap the target Power marker with the next higher marker; if it is already highest, swap any other pair.
answers.evidence: Parliament policy table.

answers.answer: Starting with the PM and going clockwise, each £1 of family cash buys one vote, in addition to printed card votes. A card’s votes can be used only once during the entire vote, across all rounds: rotate it when used and leave it rotated until vote resolution. Adjust support up or down. The PM may call another full round or stop after each round; a round with no votes must end voting. Finally restore every used card to its regular orientation after either outcome.
answers.evidence: Voting and Resolution paragraphs.

answers.answer: A player who voted for may later oppose; after opposing, they cannot vote for during that vote. Track opposition votes: the biggest opponent holds Opposition Leader, and on a tie the current holder retains it. With the recipient’s consent, votes may be cast for someone who already opposed or commits to oppose, and count toward that person’s opposition total. The PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing, except when forced to use the “Vote with my enterprises” promise.
answers.evidence: Voting paragraph.

answers.answer: On the final turn, pay upkeep for prizes as usual, then skip Refresh and go to Final Scoring. Upkeep is paid separately for each family member on a prize; if unpaid, return that member and lose that prize’s printed VP. On nonfinal turns, Refresh returns writers on orders to their associated Presidency’s Writers box; returns filled tokens and Presidency dividers and extra ships to supply; reactivates exhausted Army officers and regiments; exhausts active local alliances without reactivating them; leaves fatigue on fitted player ships; then advances the turn marker and begins London Season.
answers.evidence: Upkeep and Refresh paragraph and table.

answers.answer: Each shareholder may take one additional retirement per London Season from supply rather than Pensioners, regardless of how many firms they own. Actual cash spent after spouse discounts cannot exceed the highest total dividend marker of any firm where they own a share; printed prize cost may be higher if discounts cover the difference. A firm with no marker or a zero marker allows no retirement. Spouse discounts can enable a higher printed-cost prize; otherwise retirement rules apply, including prestige eligibility. At Final Scoring, score firms first, then allow one special retirement regardless of Company survival or failure, before ordinary final scoring; there are no display cards in Final Scoring.
answers.evidence: Special retirement paragraph.

answers.answer: Firm investment money comes from the bank to the London treasury; London pays ship acquisition, trade bids and expenses. Trade proceeds go to the India treasury, which pays dividends and expenses. Family cash cannot be transferred into or out of either firm treasury. Firm cash can move only through the specified investment, payout and expense procedures.
answers.evidence: Firms — two treasury and cash-location paragraph; firm expense/dividend procedures.

answers.answer: The Firms investment phase occurs after Family share creation and before Hiring. Investments happen without set order until nobody wants more, then strategies are chosen. The manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm; the PM resolves conflicts between firms.
answers.evidence: Firms phase: investments opening paragraph.

answers.answer: A firm may fit a ship from its own or another player’s shipyard only with that shipyard owner’s consent; pay £3 from the firm’s London treasury to the bank. A firm may buy a player-owned ship already in the Company with its owner’s consent: an unfatigued ship costs £3 and a fatigued ship £2, paid into the Shipping treasury. Firms cannot acquire Company ships or extra ships.
answers.evidence: Firms phase — Ships bullet.

answers.answer: Only a player who manages no firm at all may initiate a hostile takeover; managing a different firm also makes the player ineligible. Obtain consent from holders of a majority of the target firm’s shares. Move the target’s ships, money and shares to the initiating player’s charter, and copy both cube positions. The former manager returns the cubes and flips their family board to its family side.
answers.evidence: Firms phase — Hostile takeover bullet.

answers.answer: A merger requires managers to negotiate with every shareholder’s consent. The firm with the highest Value is primary; if tied, players choose among the tied firms. Transfer all secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to the primary and return secondary boards to their family sides; players may negotiate share transfers. If the primary would exceed ten shares, return excess shares to their owners’ supplies with those owners’ consent. The entire agreement is one binding immediate transfer, and the primary’s Value/dividend track continues.
answers.evidence: Firms phase — Merger bullet.

answers.answer: A firm may choose Hobnob with no bid, trade or dividends. It still pays expenses and retains its previous dividend marker for retirement. Hobnob firm ships are exempt from storms.
answers.evidence: Firm strategy table; firm expenses/dividends paragraph; storm eligibility table.

answers.answer: Yes. Emergency investments follow normal Company-share/workshop rules even when the ten-share cap prevents creating more shares: they pay expenses, any remaining cash is lost, and Value drops one space per emergency investment. The restriction against using shares created this turn still applies, even if those shares were traded away.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends — emergency investments; Invest bullet.

answers.answer: An emergency negotiated merger may involve only one other firm. The normal merger procedure still applies, including consent from every involved shareholder. The other firm must first pay its own expenses if it has not already done so, then cover the endangered firm’s unpaid expenses.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends — emergency merger sentence.

answers.answer: Voluntary dissolution requires all shareholders’ consent. Use the same procedure as for an insolvent firm: shares go to Debtor’s Prison for −1 VP each, ships return to their matching shipyards, and the charter flips to its family side. Workshops stay invested for the rest of the game.
answers.evidence: Firms phase — Voluntary dissolution bullet.

answers.answer: Before ordinary Power, Court or final-outcome scoring, each player adds VP from all shares they hold across all their firms, then rounds that player’s total down once. Deduct 1 VP per own family piece in Debtor’s Prison. Then permit one eligible firm special retirement before ordinary scoring. These firm scoring steps apply whether the Company survived or failed. Each firm share’s VP depends on the firm’s Value: 1 = −1, 2 = 0, 3–4 = ½, 5–7 = 1, 8–9 = 1½, and 10 = 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Final Scoring order table; Firm-track VP per share schedule.

answers.answer: For each prize member: cost £2, upkeep £0, 0 VP and 0 windows; cost £4, upkeep £1, 2 VP and 1 window; cost £8, upkeep £2, 4 VP and 2 windows; cost £14, upkeep £3, 8 VP and 3 windows; cost £20, upkeep £4, 12 VP and 4 windows.
answers.evidence: Prizes table.

answers.answer: 1710 runs turns 1–5 and has no deregulation procedures. 1758 runs turns 3–7; it starts with a Company monopoly and deregulation can be voted in. 1813 runs turns 5–8 and begins deregulated. Long 1710 runs turns 1–8, starts like 1710, and makes deregulation available separately.
answers.evidence: Scenario scope and scenario figures table.

answers.answer: In 1710, initial Standing is £10 expectations, Debt 0, each office treasury £3, initial law Royal Protection, one regiment per Army, and no Company ships. In 1758, initial Standing is £12 expectations, Debt 3, each office treasury £4, initial law Calico Acts, one regiment per Army, and one Company ship in East Indian; place the Bengal control token in the Bengal Presidency.
answers.evidence: Scenario figures table; 1758 Bengal control token clause.

answers.answer: For 1813, set initial Standing to £10 expectations and Debt 0; put £3 in each office treasury; use Military Oversight, Deregulation (Debtor’s Prison side) and Calico Acts; place two regiments per Army and one Company ship per sea zone. Put the +2/−2 share-value token in Court, create China, and put Bombay, Madras and Bengal control tokens in their Presidencies. Return the Governor General law to the box, place its office overlay over Director of Trade, use Governor General instead of Director, and use no Governors. Copy the India towers, flags, closed orders and Elephant from the scenario card’s reverse.
answers.evidence: Scenario figures table and 1813 setup paragraph.

answers.answer: The Power awards for first and second are 3/1 VP if the final turn is 1–3, 5/2 if it is 4–6, and 8/4 if it is 7–8. A tied-first group receives only the lower award each, with no other award.
answers.evidence: Power award paragraph.

answers.answer: Initial Power positions are Social at 2, Company shares at 1, and Shipping and Manufacturing at 0. Standing expectations run £4/6/8/10/12/14/16, and reset S is above £10. A lined Standing space of £4/6/8 or Debt of 5/6/7/8 permits the PM to call the special Deregulation vote; a starred Standing £4 or Debt 8 requires the PM to call it.
answers.evidence: Setup — Power and Standing positions paragraph.

answers.answer: No. The designer ruling says unrest does not add to the primary Foreign Invasion attack strength or determine resulting tower levels. Use the ordinary attack die for both attack strength and halving to create towers. On success, close all target orders once; if they are already all closed, Cascade instead. Region Loss does not close them a second time; its additional closure applies only to a normal Invasion Crisis.
answers.evidence: FAQ — Foreign Invasion and unrest ruling.

answers.answer: If Mercantile or Diplomatic Connection reduces a check to zero dice, it means failure. Company Fraud is played at the start of Revenue: roll one die per your officeholder, reduce Balance by twice the highest roll (minimum zero), and take cash from the bank equal to the actual Balance reduction, so the payout cannot exceed the cash removed from Balance. Public Demands Impeachment returns the member to supply and the office card to vacancies. Military Oversight demotes one Commander to an officer, then appoints a Commander from officers; the same former Commander remains eligible to become Commander again. These are card-specific effects.
answers.evidence: FAQ — Company Fraud payout cap and applicable official errata paragraph.

answers.answer: For shared setup, set Company Balance to £5 and family VP markers to zero. Put local alliances in their named Army boxes and loot tokens money-side up in matching regions. Choose a scenario and follow its setup card for Standing, Debt, treasuries, laws, regiments, ships and political map of India; set the Turn marker to its date and point the PM dial arm to the matching date. The scenario sets the final turn.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–2.

answers.answer: Each normal turn is London Season → Family → Firms (if deregulated) → Hiring → Company Operation → Bonuses → Revenue → Events in India → Parliament Meets → Upkeep and Refresh. Eligible special Deregulation votes occur at the very start, before London Season. London Season is skipped on the first turn of the game.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure paragraph.

answers.answer: Retirements start with the Chairman, or the former Chairman if that office is vacant, then proceed clockwise. Each player may retire each pensioner to a prize; retirement is optional, and unused Pensioners do not remain for another turn. Pay the printed cost, move the member to the prize and gain its printed VP. Set actual spending aside until London Season ends to establish display-selection order, then pay it to the bank.
answers.evidence: London Season — Retirements paragraph.

answers.answer: Whenever an empire loses its last dominated region, remove the surviving capital’s starred flag so it is no longer an empire. This applies regardless of cause, including Rebellion or Company conquest of that last dominated region.
answers.evidence: India terminology — empire definition and last-dominated-region rule.

answers.answer: Firm Value gives each share: Value 1 = −1 VP; 2 = 0 VP; 3 = ½ VP; 4 = ½ VP; 5 = 1 VP; 6 = 1 VP; 7 = 1 VP; 8 = 1½ VP; 9 = 1½ VP; 10 = 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Firm-track VP per share schedule.

answers.answer: The Family phase starts with the Chairman title holder, then proceeds clockwise, with each player resolving their family action. After all family actions, if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one, repeating while both remain. With no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible, preserving order.
answers.evidence: Family phase opening and New Company shares paragraph.

answers.answer: Follow the red ribbon: Chairman → Director of Trade (or Governor General) → Manager of Shipping → Military Affairs → Bombay Presidency → Madras Presidency → Bengal Presidency → China Superintendent, if created. Skip each vacant office. Within each Presidency, its President chooses the order of Commander, Governors and Trade; each position finishes before the next acts. Offices created by actions go into Vacant Offices unless immediate hiring is specified, and a new Governorship normally waits for a later Hiring phase. China acts after Bengal.
answers.evidence: Company Operation sequence and Presidency-order paragraphs.

answers.answer: At the start of Events in India, roll the storm die. A sea-zone result affects that zone, three storms affect all sea zones, and no storm indication means no storm checks. The die face also sets the number of India events. Resolve all required storms before drawing any event; then flip and resolve one tile at a time from the draw stack, for as many events as printed on the die face. For each eligible ship roll once: 1–2 nothing; 3–4 fatigue, or sink if already fatigued; 5–6 sink. Company and extra ships are exempt; player-owned ships in Company fleets are checked in affected zones; China ships count Eastern; firm ships count in their strategy zone; Hobnob firm ships are exempt.
answers.evidence: Events opening paragraph and Storms eligibility/roll rules.

answers.answer: For an ordinary Elephant-located Crisis, the Elephant’s tail is the attacker or acting region and its head is the defender. A sovereign actor (large capital flag or unflagged dome) causes Invasion; a dominated actor (small flag or no dome) causes Rebellion against its sovereign. If the Elephant is fully inside a Company region, resolve Rebellion against the Company. A region’s tower levels are its strength; the dome adds none. Sovereign regions have a dome without a flag or a capital/star flag; dominated regions have a small flag or no dome.
answers.evidence: India terminology; ordinary Crisis classifier.
